summary: SIEM handshake and per-event enrichment sample: reversible pseudonymization + delivery manifest for Tier-1 bank
description:
Issue summary: Cobalt Bank requires an on-demand sample delivery that demonstrates per-event enrichment (customer-side fields), reversible pseudonymization for PII, and an HMAC-wrapped delivery manifest supporting their SOC ingestion team. They also require the signed handshake (mutual TLS and certificate digest) and a small sample of live-format events mapped to their field names for ingestion testing.

Impact: Blocking onboarding verification for Cobalt Bank's SIEM team. They will not complete SOC acceptance until they can validate a sample ingest and confirm how reversible pseudonymization mapping works with their escrow process. This prevents go-live for Redwood Private (VPC) at their environment.

Requested deliverables: 1) A 5k-event sample (ndjson) with: per-event context fields (tenant_id, request_id, route, model_version), pseudonymized user identifiers with reversible mapping log, per-event HMAC header, and a manifest.json signing the batch with key thumbprint. 2) Documentation snippet showing how reversible pseudonymization key rotation and escrow works (short, operational). 3) TLS certificate digest used during the SFTP/HTTPS handshake and an example curl command showing mutual TLS succeed. 4) A short mapping crosswalk from Redwood audit field names to Cobalt Bank's target schema (CSV).

Customer asks for an on-platform sample (not synthetic) but limited to metadata and pseudonymized identifiers only — no raw prompt text or model outputs.

Preferred delivery method: SFTP upload to customer-provided host with pre-shared account OR signed HTTP PUT to their secured endpoint; preference is SFTP with resume tokens.

Acceptance criteria: sample contains all headers required by the customer's parser, HMACs verify using provided verification key, reversible pseudonymization mapping is present and can be tested by the customer's escrow team, and TLS digest matches advertised certificate used during transfer.
steps_to_reproduce: N/A — request is for packaged sample and documentation. Operational steps taken: (1) Recreate audit export pipeline on staging with tenant flags; (2) Run pseudonymization transform using escrow key; (3) Produce manifest and compute HMAC per event; (4) Upload to customer's SFTP staging host; (5) Provide verification instructions and keys.

investigation_notes: Validated pseudonymization path: transform service 'audit-redact-v2' applied with opaque_id:psn_<seed> pattern.
Key escrow: using KMS wrapped key; provided exported KEK thumbprint and rotation schedule to customer in draft doc.
Manifest signing: used staging RSA2048 key from /etc/redwood/keys/siem-export-staging.pem; signature algorithm sha256-with-rsa.
HMAC algorithm: sha256 with per-tenant shared secret (HKDF derived) — verification key shared over secure channel.
Telemetry: no errors in pipeline; CPU and I/O within expected range for batch generation (profiling attached to internal issue SUP-673902).
resolution: Workaround/partial resolution: Delivered iterative sample bundles (500-event, then 5k-event) via SFTP and provided verification keys, manifest, and short escrow documentation. Customer validated HMAC on a subset; final ingest pending full-run confirmation. Assigned owner for playbook: Diego Alvarez.
